target_customer: Demand generation and field marketing teams at enterprises running events
problem: Marketers struggled to manage event logistics and measure event engagement as part of the customer journey.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for event marketing management

founders.name: Alex Patriquin
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists no founders. IPS News (August 2020) names him founder and CEO of EventGeek and Circa.

technical_complexity.rationale: Event data aggregation and CRM integrations such as Salesforce and Marketo are standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: CRM and marketing automation integrations create some switching cost, but event software is a crowded category in sources seen.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition by an incumbent found. The 2020 pandemic forced a pivot to virtual events.

market_need_then: No 2016 demand evidence was found. By 2020 the company said its software helped convert 40,000 in-person events into virtual ones, and Okta is named as a customer.

branding.domain_note: circa.co redirects to simplecirca.com; the name collides with the defunct Circa news app (shut down June 2015).

rebrands.why: The pandemic ended in-person conferences and the founder relocated to Santa Fe and relaunched around virtual events; no reason for the specific new name was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand; sources show a rename in 2020 and name confusion with an unrelated news app.

pivots.why: COVID-19 largely eliminated large in-person conferences, per IPS News.

outcome_analysis: The company launched as EventGeek, relaunched as Circa in August 2020 after the pandemic hit in-person events, and still operates with about 21 people. No credible funding or exit was found, so success or failure cannot be judged from public sources. The pandemic pivot kept it alive and gave it enterprise customers like Okta.
notes: circa.co redirected to simplecirca.com and that page was not fetched. Funding: aggregators (Bouncewatch, Seedtable, Dealroom) mention an August 2016 angel round, a 2021 pre-seed of 500K and a 2021 seed, but with conflicting amounts and no named outlet, so they are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The YC page says Boston while press says the company moved to Santa Fe in 2020. The outcome search surfaced only the unrelated Circa news app. No dated competitor source from 2016 was found; Okta is a customer not a competitor. Completeness pass: funding gap is known (aggregators mention angel and seed rounds) but amounts and dates conflict and none could be verified or attributed to this company, so no round is recorded.
